html:
The Armenian diaspora is the large community of Armenians living outside Armenia, larger than the population of the country itself, which took its modern shape after the Armenian genocide of 1915.

Armenian merchant colonies existed for centuries, from Lviv and Venice to New Julfa and India. The survivors of 1915 spread to Syria, Lebanon, France and the United States, and many later moved on from the Middle East. After 1991 emigration from poor independent Armenia sent many to Russia. The diaspora built churches, schools and newspapers, campaigned for recognition of the genocide, and gave Armenia money and political support, notably in the Karabakh conflict. Among its famous members are the singer Charles Aznavour and the writer William Saroyan. It ties Armenia to the world.
sum: The Armenian diaspora is the large community of Armenians living outside Armenia, larger than the population of the country itself, which took its modern shape after the Armenian genocide of 1915.
